record.
2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant and the learned Additional Government Advocate for the State.

3. As per learned counsel for the applicant, the present applicant Bhaskar Singh is in jail since 23.02.2024 in Case Crime No.449 of 2023, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC, Police Station-Kotwali Nagar, District-Ayodhya.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the present applicant has been falsely implicated in this case as he has not committed any offence as alleged in the prosecution story.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant has further submitted that allegations so levelled against in the F.I.R is not probable, in as much as, the complainant has not stated in the FIR that his Aadhar card and Pan card was lost and the present applicant has any how found that Aadhar card and Pan card to avail the finance facility from Bajaj Finance.

If the Aadhar card and Pan card of the informant had been lost any complaint to that effect would have been lodged by the informant but no such complaint to that effect has been lodged by the informant.
It has not been indicated in the FIR as to how the present applicant has utilised or found the Adhar card and Pan card of the informant.
The impugned FIR has lodged by the complainant having ulterior motive and extraneous design in his mind so as to use financed amount.
Attention has been drawn towards supplementary affidavit showing Annexure no.2 which is statement of Risk Manager of the Bajaj Finance to the effect that the loan account in question has been closed.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant has further submitted that mobile in question, for which, the amount was financed from Bajaj Finance has not been recovered from the present applicant nor any relevant material or evidence has been found during investigation to suggest that the present applicant is beneficiary of the finance.
The charge sheet has been filed.
The present applicant have no criminal history.

He undertakes that if the applicant is released on bail he shall not misuse the liberty of bail, if so granted by this Court and shall abide by all terms and conditions of the bail order and shall cooperate with the trial proceedings properly.
7. Learned Additional Government Advocate has, however, opposed the prayer for bail but he has not disputed the aforesaid submission of learned counsel for the applicant.

8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, perusing the material available on record and also considering the nature of allegations, arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, I find it a fit case for bail.
The bail application is, therefore, allowed.

9. Let the applicant-Bhaskar Singh be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. and (iv) the applicant shall not leave India without prior permission of the court.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
